summary: Chris Plante reviews Valve's Steam Deck OLED for Polygon, arguing it improves far more than the screen despite identical processing power to the original. The HDR OLED display, 30-50% longer battery life, faster Wi-Fi, a dedicated Bluetooth module, better haptics and touchscreen, and faster charging make it a standout handheld. Prices stay the same as the original Steam Deck with more storage, and Plante calls it his favorite console ever.
one_line: Polygon's review finds the Steam Deck OLED a major upgrade through its HDR screen, battery life and many small hardware improvements, despite unchanged power.
key_facts: The Steam Deck OLED is identical in raw power to the original Steam Deck; Valve says this gives developers a single optimization target.
Valve hopes to release the Steam Deck 2 in two to three years and promises a generational power leap.
The OLED screen is the first HDR OLED on any gaming portable, with peak brightness of 1,000 nits for HDR content and 600 nits for SDR, versus 400 nits on the original.
The display is 7.4 inches versus 7 inches on the original, with smaller bezels, a 110% DCI-P3 color gamut and a 90 Hz refresh rate, short of the Asus ROG Ally's 120 Hz.
Valve promises 30-50% more battery life than the original running the latest firmware, not the early firmware.
The Steam Deck OLED adds a Wi-Fi 6E radio and a dedicated Bluetooth module, enabling better wireless audio, waking from a controller and many Bluetooth controllers for multiplayer.
The new power supply charges from 20% to 80% in 45 minutes and has a 2.5-meter cable; parts will again be sold through iFixit.
Valve has shipped around 300 hardware-improving updates since launch, and the original Steam Deck will get a BIOS update with a smaller battery improvement.
Prices: $649 for 1 TB OLED, $529 for 512 GB OLED, and $399 for the 256 GB non-OLED model (up from 64 GB).
A limited-edition 1 TB Steam Deck OLED with a translucent shell costs $679 and is only available in the U.S. and Canada.
Plante tested the game Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name on high settings at 60 fps and played for hours without plugging in the charger.
The Steam Deck OLED goes on sale Nov. 16 through the Steam storefront, and the reviewer used a unit provided by Valve.
